title: Royal letters patent for Law's bank
established: Manuscript letters patent authorized Banque Générale. The museum identifies signing by Louis XV and Regent Philippe d'Orléans. Full French clauses require manuscript examination.
limitations: The charter's existence and institutional purpose are supported; loan disbursements, personal investors and full wording are not verified.

title: Order restricting paper-for-large-silver-coin exchange
established: The Council of State order restricted exchange of banknotes for large silver coins during Law's crisis.
limitations: An order is not a record of how many coins were actually exchanged, nor proof of any particular counterparty.

title: Royal order to inventory and burn designated banknotes
established: The edict names Baussan and Bertin as officials tasked with reporting on specified notes and ensuring their destruction.
limitations: No banknote destruction totals or completed burning certificates extracted from the original manuscript.

title: Hutcheson public letter challenging South Sea stock calculations
reference: Wellcome work yy3prd74; ECCO edition
established: A pamphlet by Archibald Hutcheson responds to share valuation printed in the White-Hall Evening-Post.
limitations: The bibliographic record identifies a public discussion, but no original numerical calculation or private recipient communication has been transcribed.

title: Satire showing John Law and Amsterdam's English coffee house
reference: Wellcome 811589i
established: An etching depicts share traders in an English coffee house in Amsterdam and includes a bust of John Law and the Parisian Quincampoix street reference.
limitations: Images satirize market life; depicted individuals or transactions must not be treated as verified actual trades.

title: Surviving Dutch Leydse Courant market coverage, 1719–1720
reference: Yale ICF 1720 Project, Leydse Courant image archive
established: Digitized issues cover 20 November 1719 through 30 December 1720, offering a dated source to test when news was printed in Dutch markets.
limitations: This atlas has not extracted any issue's specific quoted prices or communications; no information-lag estimate is claimed.

title: Stad Rotterdam transaction book begins recording financial activity
reference: Yale ICF, Stad Rotterdam Transaction Book, pp.1–300, July 16–24 1720
established: Yale indexes original Rotterdam discount-company transactions starting July 16, 1720 and books extending to 1723, which offer a route for reconstructing counterparties.
limitations: No named counterparty, transaction value or British/French security purchase is asserted without reading the ledger page.

title: Passenger list for Louisiana, January 1720–January 1721
reference: ANOM COL G1 464, 68 images, record 31224
established: Archive listing identifies a list of people registered for Louisiana voyages from Lorient over January 1720–January 1721.
limitations: The listing itself does not prove that each individual embarked, survived, was free or enslaved, arrived, or settled. Do not derive demographic totals.

place: Biloxi (Fort Louis de la Mobile vicinity)
title: Diron census of Mobile and surrounding settlements
reference: ANOM COL G1 464, 7 images, record 31234
established: Archive catalogue identifies a census organized by households, people categorized as servants/enslaved, and livestock.
limitations: The colonial categories dehumanized enslaved people and do not convey their names or experiences equally. Totals remain unverified.

title: Census of New Orleans and nearby concessions, appended to Diron's letter
reference: ANOM COL G1 464, 12 images, record 31235; attached letter dated 1722-01-02
established: A signed census reports people, French servants, enslaved laborers, and agricultural conditions; metadata identifies Diron and co-signers.
limitations: Neither demographic totals nor individual identity matches have been extracted, and colonial counts may exclude independent Indigenous communities.

title: English-language printed account explicitly describing Mr Law's Mississippi Company
reference: BnF Gallica ark:/12148/bpt6k109867v (scan fetch denied)
established: The BnF curated list identifies a 1720 English-language account of the French Mississippi Company, direct evidence that an English-language explanation circulated in print.
limitations: Publication place, author, readership, full argument, and involvement of South Sea directors remain unverified in this research pass.

title: Signed one-page manuscript acknowledging 20 bank-equity shares
reference: HNOC MSS 606 Folder 4, accession 2010.0158.20, PDF finding aid printed p. 2
established: Frenier signed a document certifying an unidentified bearer received twenty shares from Mr. Imbert, the Duke of Orléans's first valet. This is a verified archive description of a distinct 1719 financial instrument.
limitations: Full French note, price paid, previous holder's ownership and identity of the bearer were not independently read or established. Not evidence of an illicit coordinated network.

title: Original 50-livre Banque Générale bearer banknote
reference: HNOC MSS 606 Folder 3, accession 2010.0158.19, PDF finding aid printed p. 2
established: The archive lists an original banknote for fifty livres tournois, serial number handwritten, signed in print at Paris on September 2, 1720 by five named officials and promising payment to bearer.
limitations: Face value and promised redemption are not a record that any bearer redeemed the note. Names of actual holders, cash exchanged and later valuation have not been checked.

title: Second, expanded 1721 New Orleans census copy — ANOM 31236
reference: ANOM COL G1 464, 17-page catalogued document / 29 digital images; CABAC_PIAF_6928; item 31236
established: Archival catalogue explicitly labels this as apparently a copy of the previous 1721 New Orleans census, followed by more extensive information on land concessions and colony status.
limitations: No handwritten original folio, totals or population categories checked; this is a likely duplicate or extended companion and must not be counted as a second independent 1721 census.

title: Le Gac memoir: five parts including Indigenous and French village names
reference: ANOM FR CAOM 4DFC8, item 40699, 101-page memoir / 99 digital images
established: The colonial Company official Le Gac's memoir describes Louisiana at his arrival in 1718, his activities to 1721 and lists French and Indigenous villages on the Mississippi and tributaries.
limitations: The memoir's actual village names and descriptions are not independently extracted from the French manuscript. The official's reporting is not equivalent to Indigenous self-description or community-approved knowledge.

title: French letters describing Sainte-Catherine concession conflict with Natchez
reference: ANOM COL G1 465, item 31377, four digitized images, letters March 9–10 1722
established: Archival catalogue describes letters from French officers concerning an attack on the Sainte-Catherine concession by Natchez people and French armed-response discussions.
limitations: Only French administrative and settler perspectives in the catalogue have been inspected; no Natchez perspective, exact casualty numbers, or guilt conclusions can be established from this title.

title: Superior Council sends Choctaw trade concerns to Company of Indies
reference: Historic New Orleans Collection manuscript guide; AC C13, vol.9 p.51, 47-page copy, dated 1725-02-27; see separate C13A vol.9 fol.65v in Musco et al. (2025)
established: An archival guide describes a letter from the Louisiana Superior Council covering Choctaw trade alongside other colonial issues. Specific text and folios have not been inspected; relation to scholarship's French translation should be checked.
limitations: The 47-page original is not transcribed or quoted here. No original 1725 Choctaw petitions have been directly accessed and no Company decision or treasury disbursement is implied.

title: Diron d'Artaguiette correspondence on Périer and the Choctaw mission
reference: HNOC manuscript guide, AC C13 vol.12 p.362, nine-page original dated February 9–10 1730
established: The archive guide describes Diron's letter to the Controller General discussing Régis du Roullet's Choctaw visit, related conflict with Périer, and regional conditions. The date range is preserved.
limitations: The full original French nine pages have not been read, and the abstract does not verify financial award, local trade prices or actual compensation.

title: Ministerial letter to Salmon covers Company-enslaved people sale reference and Diron–Company case
reference: HNOC Surrey Calendar item 7620; AC B57:815 / ANOM B57:815; two-page letter, Minister of Marine to Salmon, 2 September 1732, Marly. HNOC also lists microfilm at the Library of Congress, Center for Louisiana Studies (reel identifier not supplied).
established: The HNOC catalogue abstract lists Macmahon's sale of people enslaved by the Company and, as a separate subject, approval of a Superior Council decision in the Diron–Company of Indies case. It identifies a two-page ministerial letter dated 2 September 1732 at Marly, with archival citation B57:815. This establishes what the catalogue describes, not the unexamined letter's operative text or the sale's details.
limitations: Only the HNOC catalogue abstract was examined; the two-page letter was not. The letter date is not a verified sale date. The abstract supplies no names, count, purchaser, price, receipt, payment, transfer terms or legal basis, and does not connect the sale subject to the Diron decision or the 24 February 1731 debt decree. The catalogue uses a period racial term; the atlas refers to people enslaved by the Company and does not infer their consent, identities or community affiliation.

title: Council folios cited for 29,000-livre monopoly compensation award
reference: ANOM C13A, 1732, folios 33–33v as cited by Musco, Ellis & Spring (2025) — original image not independently opened
established: A peer-reviewed study explicitly refers to the archival folios and describes a 29,000 French-livre compensation judgment for Bernard Diron d'Artaguiette after a challenged trade monopoly.
limitations: Only modern scholarly description of the archival folios inspected. The archival hand itself, judgment language, date and actual payment are all unverified.

title: Local 24-page French Superior Council retrocession dossier
reference: Louisiana Historical Center record 1731-01-24-03, 24-page French Superior Council dossier, https://lacolonialdocs.org/document/2003. Record page displays Pg. 1 / 24 and 48 Image links; three sampled targets resolve to small station_thumbs_sm JPEG previews (see data/louisiana_image_access_audit.json).
established: The Louisiana Historical Center record page identifies a French Superior Council item dated 24 January 1731, originating in New Orleans, and categorizes it as Administrative Acts, Retrocession of Louisiana. It displays 24 pages and 48 Image links; three sampled image targets are thumbnail previews. The index lists Coligny, the Company of Indies, Le Redde and Orry. This establishes archival metadata and preview-link availability, not the contents of the handwritten clauses.
limitations: No French text was transcribed. Only three of the 48 Image links were sampled; all three returned small JPEG thumbnail previews under station_thumbs_sm, and no full-resolution page asset was verified. Do not infer that the 48 links represent recto/verso pairs or a particular page sequence. No WPA Black Book 20 crosswalk has been verified. The archive's modern category 'Retrocession of Louisiana' is not a transcription of operative language. The 24 January local record date is distinct from the 23 January royal decree and does NOT establish final Crown retrocession or an effective handover date.

title: Council of State decree concerning the retrocession of Louisiana and Illinois
reference: 1731 Imprimerie royale printed decree, 3 printed pages, reproduced in CIHM/ICMH microfiche (1985) from a copy supplied by Seminary of Quebec Library; PDF page indices 4–6; compare contemporary Mercure de France, March 1731, pp. 610–611 (Bureau du Mercure OCR); ANOM COL F3 242 fol. 187 remains an unexamined manuscript locator.
established: Direct visual examination of the three printed pages in the 1985 CIHM/ICMH microfiche reproduction confirms the act is dated 23 January 1731 and printed by the Imprimerie royale. The decree accepts the Company's retrocession, made by its syndics and directors on its behalf, of the property, seigneurie and justice of Louisiana and its dependencies and the country of the Illinois; it also lists the places, forts, buildings, artillery, arms and troops then present. It accepts the return of the Company's exclusive-trade privilege and declares Louisiana commerce free to the King's subjects. In the same text, the Company is maintained in its rights against debtors in the province, exercisable as it judges appropriate. This is Company-side creditor-rights language, not a named debtor, a quantified claim, a Company liability, a Crown assumption, or proof of collection or payment.
limitations: The accessible witness is a 1985 22X microfiche reproduction of a copy supplied by the Seminary of Quebec Library; its own technical notes flag discoloured/show-through pages. The physical 1731 copy and ANOM COL F3 242 fol. 187 were not examined. The transcription is from visual reading of the three facsimile pages, checked against extracted OCR, not a new examination of the physical original. The phrase about the Company not being charged in future follows the return of the exclusive-trade privilege and must not be treated as an omnibus discharge of separate Company debts. The separate 24 February 1731 debt decree remains unread. This French Crown/Company instrument does not establish Indigenous consent to French territorial claims or describe the perspectives of Illinois/Illini nations; it does not identify enslaved people or establish that people were included among the listed material assets. No debtor identities, amounts, enforcement, collection, receipt, payment, settlement or Crown assumption of Company liabilities is established.

title: Salmon reports royal possession of former Company forts, buildings, artillery
reference: HNOC Guide to French Louisiana Manuscripts item 7287; ANOM C13,15:31; two pages; dated January 19, 1732
established: Salmon's indexed letter reports taking physical possession of specified Company assets for the King, with exceptions at Illinois, Natchitoches and site written 'Youanis (Yazoo)', plus dispute over stores.
limitations: The original letter has not been read; 'Youanis (Yazoo)' is not verified as the Haiyowvni/Youanis Choctaw post, and the index does not prove that every asset was transferred or debts settled.

title: Company's Louisiana debt decree dated February 24, 1731 (printed in 1733)
reference: BnF Catalogue général: 1731 Imprimerie royale printing (filtered result 39, Acte 1731-02-24 Versailles); BnF Gallica ark:/12148/btv1b8602624n: 1733 printing; Columbia Law rare book 1505745: 1733 Paris Saugrain–Prault edition of the same 1731-02-24 act. Historical catalogue leads: Louisiana Historical Society, 1903 Colonial Exhibit catalogue, printed p.17, items 342 (23 Jan retrocession) and 345 (24 Feb debt decree), both credited to Mr. Gaspar Cusachs; Exposition Française de la Louisiane, 1904, printed p.21, item 72 lists the debt decree title/date without an item-level owner. BnF four-volume Recueil notice ark:/12148/cb338513279 (FRBNF33851327) remains a separate, unexamined retrieval route. Related LHC retrieval audit: RG377 accession T025.2003.112 (photocopied Library of Congress holdings; published contents list checked for 24 Feb 1731) and RG3 accessions 1852.30/1852.36; RG1 creditor/manumission collection-level lead. These are related archival routes, not identified witnesses to the 24 Feb decree. UW Libraries History Digital Collections guide lists LLMC Digital behind an authenticated UW proxy; Columbia's LLMC record 1338688796 availability in the UW instance is not confirmed. RG377 also lists 13 Aug 1729 in-kind supply terms and 30 Aug/6 Sep 1729 account-balancing/examination records (records 1729081301, 1729083001 and 1729090601); these are related financial-administration leads, not the 1731 debt decree. Related post-retrocession retrieval lead only: LHC record 1736-08-20-04, index card #6022, reports a receipt involving Jean Labbe, Guillon and a card-reported 5,845-livre Company indebtedness; this is not an identified witness to the 1731 decree.
established: Two bibliographically distinct printings are indexed for the same royal debt decree dated 24 February 1731: BnF lists a 1731 Imprimerie royale edition and a Gallica-linked 1733 edition, while Columbia Law catalogues a two-page 1733 Saugrain–Prault printing. This does not imply two separate laws. Separately, the 1903 Louisiana Historical Society loan-exhibit catalogue lists the 24 February decree as item 345 on printed p.17 and attributes it to Mr. Gaspar Cusachs; the same page lists the 23 January retrocession decree as item 342 with the same catalogue attribution. A 1904 Exposition Française de la Louisiane catalogue independently lists a debt decree with the same title/date as item 72 on printed p.21. These later catalogues establish historical exhibit/listing references only, not current custody, physical-copy identity, operative clauses or payment.
limitations: Original operative clauses of either printing were not read; Gallica scan access was denied and the 1731 BnF catalogue result has no stable item-level permalink. No identified legal debtor, Crown assumption of corporate liabilities, debt amount, payment or actual disbursement is proven. The 1903 catalogue's Owner column is a historical attribution to Mr. Gaspar Cusachs, not a current location or complete chain of custody. The 1904 catalogue gives no item-level owner for item 72; its general preface thanks G. Cusachs for access to collections, but that does not justify assigning item 72 to him. The two catalogues do not prove that their entries refer to the same physical copy or to any BnF/Columbia/LLMC witness. The 1755–1756 BnF Recueil remains a separate unexamined retrieval route: its T.4 chronological table is catalogued, but no volume or index contents were read and the decree's presence in the Recueil is unverified. No debtor, amount, collection, receipt, payment, settlement or Crown assumption is established. The Louisiana State Museum Historical Center's RG377 finding aid (accession T025.2003.112) was examined: no 24 February 1731 item appears in its published contents list; the last listed item is a 28 February 1731 sailing instruction in Box 8. The summary states 9 boxes, but the online contents list has no Box 9 heading. This unresolved inventory discrepancy is not proof the decree is absent from the physical collection. RG3 audit/bookkeeping records and RG1 creditor/manumission records are related research leads only; no direct link to the 1731 decree, completed audit, actual balance, enforcement, payment or settlement is established. The UW guide confirms an authenticated LLMC Digital route, but not public access or availability of LLMC1338688796 in the UW instance. The RG377 finding aid also describes a 13 Aug 1729 order for Company-supplied enslaved people with payment terms in tobacco or local produce, plus 30 Aug and 6 Sep 1729 account-balancing/examination instructions. These are catalogue summaries only; no delivery, receipt, completed audit, account balance or payment is established, and no direct legal link to the 24 Feb 1731 decree is proven. The later LHC record 1736-08-20-04 and card #6022 report a receipt involving an enslaved-person sale and a 5,845-livre indebtedness attributed to Jean Labbe; its two handwritten pages remain unread, the card's account is not verified, and no direct link to this 1731 decree or actual payment is established. It is a related post-retrocession lead only.

title: Royal decree reforms Louisiana Superior Council, excluding Company directors
reference: ANOM COL F3 242 fol. 190, copy of edict dated 22 May 1731 (Ribeaux 2026, PDF p. 8 n. 39); Saadani 2003, pp. 117–118 and p. 131 n. 3, also cites AN, Archives de la Marine A1-69 fol. 20 as letters patent dated 24 May 1731, plus AN, Colonies A22 fols. 134–135; A23 fols. 106–107; B55 fols. 634–635; C13A13 fol. 260 (draft letters patent). These are scholarly archival locators; see extract-010.
established: Ribeaux (2026, PDF p. 8 n. 39) cites a copy of an edict dated 22 May 1731 at ANOM COL F3 242 fol. 190 and reports that the Superior Council's composition reverted to the 1716 arrangements, excluding Company directors; the note adds that the cited text makes no mention of judges in distant places. Saadani (2003, pp. 117–118) independently describes the disappearance of the Company-representing Conseil de régie and revocation of the August 1719 provisions allowing Company directors to sit on the Superior Council. Saadani's note 3 (p. 131) cites a related set of records, including a letters-patent reference dated 24 May 1731 at AN, Archives de la Marine A1-69 fol. 20. The relationship between the 22 May F3 242 copy and the 24 May A1-69 reference remains unresolved; this is a scholarly cross-check, not direct transcription.
limitations: No original folio or printed instrument cited here was directly examined. The 22 May 1731 date belongs to the copy cited at ANOM COL F3 242 fol. 190; Saadani's footnote separately describes a letters-patent record at AN, Archives de la Marine A1-69 fol. 20 as dated 24 May 1731. These may be related copies, distinct instruments, or a citation/date discrepancy; do not silently merge them. No individual Company directors, appointment roster, votes, detailed implementation, or continued status of judges in remote places is established. The reorganization of a French colonial court does not establish Indigenous consent or a transfer of Choctaw sovereignty. No Company property transfer, corporate debt assumption, liability, settlement, amount or payment is established.

place: New Orleans, French Louisiana (archive's collection context)
title: Company of Indies appears in indexed agreement with creditors, October 1735
reference: Louisiana Historical Center, French Superior Council collection, 1735-10-19-02, https://lacolonialdocs.org/document/2450
established: The Louisiana Colonial Documents index labels record 1735-10-19-02 'Private Documents, Agreement with Creditors' and indexes the Company of Indies alongside Lamy, Bruslé, Hugault, Prevost, Henry, Salmon and Rivard names. This establishes an indexed document lead, not the agreement's contents.
limitations: No original clause, signature, debtor, creditor, asset, settlement amount or payment has been transcribed. Indexed persons are not assigned roles or presumed to share an agreement across other documents. Compare the original French with WPA Black Book 23 (1735 July–December) only after obtaining the exact WPA page.

place: New Orleans, French Louisiana (archive's collection context)
title: LHC-indexed 1736 receipt: card #6022 describes a Company debt and an enslaved-person sale
reference: Louisiana Historical Center, French Superior Council collection, record 1736-08-20-04, https://lacolonialdocs.org/document/2689; three displayed pages. The item page lists Guillon and Labbe/Labe; separate person-index route https://lacolonialdocs.org/person/32026/for/documents/2689 also returns this record under a Guillon entry, but identity is not confirmed by the manuscript. English typed index card #6022: https://lacolonialdocs-data.s3.amazonaws.com/doc-img-800x0/doc-img-127962.jpg; two handwritten 800x0 image derivatives: https://lacolonialdocs-data.s3.amazonaws.com/doc-img-800x0/doc-img-127960.jpg and https://lacolonialdocs-data.s3.amazonaws.com/doc-img-800x0/doc-img-127961.jpg. Card cites Louisiana Historical Quarterly, vol. 8, no. 3 (July 1925), p. 489, second document; LHC's journal inventory confirms the issue but p. 489 was not examined.
established: The LHC record page dates this three-page French Superior Council item 20 August 1736, places it in New Orleans, and labels it “Private Documents, Receipt.” The item page lists Guillon, Company of Indies, Hugault, Picquery, Henry and Labbe/Labe. A separate LHC person-index route (page ID 32026) also returns this record under a Guillon entry; this is an index association, not a personal identity or role verified from the manuscript. The first displayed image is English typed index card #6022. It reads: “Receipt to Jean Labbe for price of negro sold to Guillon, which was part of the 5845 livres for which Labe was indebted to the Company.” The card therefore reports a 5,845-livre Company indebtedness and says the price connected with the sale formed part of that amount. Two handwritten manuscript-page derivatives were opened, but their text was not reliably transcribed. This is a card-level report, not a verified account balance or transaction.
limitations: Only the English typed index card #6022 and two 800x0 JPEG derivatives of handwritten manuscript pages were visually examined; the underlying French text was not reliably transcribed and the 600 dpi preservation TIFF masters were not accessed. The card's author/date and its relationship to WPA summaries are not established. Its historical word “negro” is retained only as source wording; the person described is unnamed and their voice is absent. The 5,845 livres is an index-card-reported indebtedness, not a verified account balance, legal liability, amount paid, receipt by the Company, or settlement. The card does not specify the sale price separately or establish whether proceeds were credited to the Company. The archive's category “Receipt” and the card summary are not proof that money changed hands. No relationship to the 24 February 1731 decree is established. The LHC says its initial indexing used WPA summaries and warns of omissions of enslaved people's and women's names; this specific card is not proven to be a WPA abstract, and absence from it is not evidence of absence from the manuscript. The record is a colonial administrative perspective, not the enslaved person's perspective or evidence of Indigenous consent. The separate Guillon person-index route is an index association only; it does not establish that the indexed person is the Guillon named in the card or prove a personal relationship.

place: New Orleans, French Louisiana (archive's collection context)
title: Company of Indies appears in indexed private receipt, May 1737

place: New Orleans, French Louisiana (archive's collection context)
title: Duval succession statement-of-account record with English index card, LHC 1732-07-15-01
reference: Louisiana Historical Center, French Superior Council collection, record 1732-07-15-01, catalogue date 15 July 1732, five displayed image assets: https://lacolonialdocs.org/document/2148 ; index card #6558: https://lacolonialdocs-data.s3.amazonaws.com/doc-img-800x0/doc-img-125822.jpg ; four handwritten image derivatives: doc-img-125818.jpg, doc-img-125819.jpg, doc-img-125820.jpg, doc-img-125821.jpg under https://lacolonialdocs-data.s3.amazonaws.com/doc-img-800x0/ .
established: The Louisiana Historical Center record page labels this a five-page French Superior Council item dated 15 July 1732 and indexes Antoine Bruslé, Prévost, the Company of Indies and the succession of François Duval. The first displayed image is English typed index card #6558. Its heading reads 'STATEMENT OF ACCOUNTS DUE FROM THE IND. CO.'; its prose says it closes François Duval's account with the Company as of 15 January 1736 and reports a balance due the Company by the succession of Sr. Duval of 101,975 livres 6 sols 2 deniers. The card attributes signatures to Bruslé on 15 July 1732 and Prévost on 15 January 1736. Four handwritten manuscript-page image derivatives were opened but not transcribed. The card's heading and prose point in different directions about who owes whom.
limitations: The record-page date 15 July 1732, the card's account-as-of date 15 January 1736 and its two stated sign-off dates are not reconciled; the record may be composite, the 1732 account may have been closed later, or the card/metadata may contain an error. The card's own author and creation date are not stated. The LHC project says initial indexing used WPA summaries from 1935–1942, but this specific card is not proven to be a WPA abstract. Its heading 'DUE FROM THE IND. CO.' conflicts with the prose 'balance due the company by the succession'; do not classify the direction as established. The 101,975 livres 6 sols 2 deniers is an index-card-reported balance, not a verified transcription of the handwritten account, legal liability, collectible receivable, payment, settlement or Crown assumption. Four handwritten image derivatives were visually inspected but their entries could not be reliably transcribed; the 600 dpi preservation TIFF masters were not accessed. No relationship to the 24 February 1731 decree is established. The LHC warns that WPA abstracts omit names of enslaved people and women; absence from this index is not evidence of absence from the underlying pages. This Company accounting record does not represent Indigenous consent or affected-community perspectives.

title: Superior Council ordinance on debts owed to the Company and commodity acceptance prices, March 1735
reference: HNOC Guide to French Louisiana Manuscripts item 8949; ANOM A 23:118; 3-page ordinance dated 30 March 1735, https://surrey.hnoc.org/full_notice.php?id_document=8949
established: The archival calendar identifies a 30 March 1735 Superior Council ordinance concerning payment of debts TO the Company of the Indies and rates for accepting furs, indigo, tobacco, cotton, pitch, tar and rice. A 1916 archival historian separately discusses dated colonial-produce prices at the royal storehouse and cites the 30 March ordinance.
limitations: Calendar abstract and secondary historian's account, NOT a transcription of the three French ordinance pages. Exact legal language, rate schedule, currency/measure details and application to any named debtor remain unverified. This is a Company-as-creditor lead, not proof the Crown assumed Company liabilities, that produce was actually delivered, or that any person paid. No demonstrated connection to the 24 February 1731 decree or 1735 October creditors' agreement. Colonial accounts omit Indigenous and enslaved people's agency and must be interpreted critically.

title: Louisiana card-money ordinance as reproduced in Zay (1892), not original 1735 folio
reference: Ernest Zay, Histoire monétaire des colonies françaises (1892), printed pp.181–183, ordinance of 14 September 1735, articles I–VI
established: The 1892 edition reproduces a royal order specifying a 200,000-livre nominal card-money fabrication ceiling, controls on official signatures and registers, and proposed acceptance at royal stores and for bills of exchange. This is a legal authorization as transmitted in a later publication.
limitations: Original 1735 ordinance, registration, manufacturing procès-verbaux, issued notes, exchange bills and receipts not inspected. The Crown's assertions about specie leaving Louisiana and inhabitants' wishes are not independently verified. A BnF-derived OCR mirror misreads the heading as 260 m. while articles I, IV, V read 200 m.; check the printed page image. This record does not concern a verified payment of the Company's 1731 debts.

title: RG3 1852.30 — resolution concerning Company-furnished enslaved people not yet paid for (finding-aid abstract)
reference: Louisiana State Museum Historical Center, French Manuscripts, Mississippi Valley, RG3, accession 1852.30; dated 11 Dec 1725; 4 pages. Collection on loan from the Louisiana Historical Society; finding aid states open for research. The 2024 LSM collection guide states RG3 has been microfilmed; reel identifier not supplied.
established: The June 2013 RG3 finding aid describes accession 1852.30 as a resolution concerning enslaved people in Louisiana who had been furnished to residents by the Company of the Indies but had not been paid for; the abstract says those residents were prohibited from selling them. This is the finding aid's summary, not a transcription of the four-page document.
limitations: Original four pages not examined. No individual people, price, account balance, legal debtor identity, actual enforcement, payment, settlement or connection to the 24 February 1731 decree is established. The finding aid uses colonial language that treats enslaved people as property; this administrative abstract is not their perspective. Pair this record with the RG1 petitions by enslaved people seeking manumission and community-aware scholarship; do not convert people into a neutral financial-flow entry.

title: RG377 1729021501 — instructions for general and special bookkeepers in Louisiana (finding-aid abstract)
reference: Louisiana State Museum Historical Center, Louisiana French Colonial Period Documents, RG377, accession T025.2003.112, record 1729021501; Series B43:846–864; 43 sheets. established: The August 2022 RG377 finding aid describes instructions dated 15 February 1729 for general and special bookkeepers in Louisiana. Its abstract says they address cashiers, warehouse keepers, maritime trade, fortifications, company housing, active and inactive debts, ship expenses, payment of debts of the 'old company', payments in silver and bills, and slave cargoes. The phrase 'old company' is not identified in the finding aid.
limitations: The 43 sheets and underlying Library of Congress originals were not examined. The finding-aid summary is not a transcription or financial statement. It establishes no named debtor, creditor balance, completed transaction, payment, settlement, Crown assumption or link to the 24 February 1731 decree. Do not equate 'old company' with a specific predecessor without reading the French text. The colonial accounting categories do not represent enslaved people's perspectives. The identity of the 'old company' is not established by the finding aid.

title: RG377 1729081301 — order for delivery of four enslaved people to Sieur D'Aquin with in-kind payment terms (finding-aid abstract)
reference: Louisiana State Museum Historical Center, Louisiana French Colonial Period Documents, RG377, accession T025.2003.112, record 1729081301; Series B43:868–869; 2 sheets. Finding aid says issued at Paris by the Company of the Indies.
established: The August 2022 RG377 finding aid describes an order to deliver four enslaved people to Sieur D'Aquin, to be paid for in tobacco or other local produce at 1,000 livres each, collected from three consecutive harvests following delivery. These are catalogue-described contractual terms, not evidence of delivery or receipt.
limitations: Finding-aid summary only; The original two sheets were not examined. No individual people are identified; no delivery, harvest collection, payment, amount paid, default, enforcement, account balance or connection to the 24 February 1731 decree is established. The livres figure is a catalogue-described price term, not a monetary payment or a verified financial flow. The colonial record treats enslaved people as property and does not convey their voices; seek related petitions and community-aware scholarship.
